```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(sppdata)
```

## What's in the SPP

The Subnational Politics Project harmonizes subnational political data for
Argentina, Brazil, and Mexico. The package exposes six relational datasets:

```{r}
spp_datasets()
```

## Exploring variables (offline)

The codebook is bundled with the package, so you can browse variables without
downloading anything:

```{r}
head(spp_codebook())

# Just one dataset:
spp_codebook("SED")
```

For a readable, printed view of a dataset's variables:

```{r}
spp_describe("SED")
```

## Downloading data

`spp_data()` fetches a dataset from the project's GitHub Releases mirror and
caches it locally, so it only hits the network once per version.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sed <- spp_data("SED")
head(sed)
```

By default you get the version this package was built against, which keeps
analyses reproducible. To pull a specific published version:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sed_v1 <- spp_data("SED", tag = "v1.0")
```

## Managing the cache

```{r, eval = FALSE}
spp_cache_dir()     # where downloads live
spp_cache_clear()   # reclaim the space
```

## Citing the data

The archival, citable copies of the datasets live on Harvard Dataverse. The
GitHub Releases mirror is a convenience download channel only.

```{r}
spp_citation()
```
